cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his beloved child, and he just told him to gently correct the people who oppose him (2 Timothy 1:1-2; 2:24-25). Now friend, this next line has BIG "close the door and have a seat" energy. Paul writes, "But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come."

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy that terrible times will come in the last days. What does he say will make them so terrible?

cards.text: So Paul starts a list, and friend, this list does NOT quit: lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy.
He's STILL going: unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, without love of good, traitorous, reckless, conceited. And I thought MY mustache went on forever.

cards.question: Paul's list started with people who love themselves and love money. Near the end, he says they'll be lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of who?
Paul says the people on this list have a form of godliness.

cards.text: They have a form of godliness, but they deny its power. That's a cookie box with a perfect gold bow on top, and you open it up and it's just... crumbs.

cards.question: These people have a form of godliness but deny its power. What does Paul tell Timothy to do about people like these?

cards.text: Paul says they're the kind who worm their way into households. They captivate vulnerable women who are weighed down with sins and led astray by various passions.

cards.question: Paul says the women these men captivate are always learning. What's the catch?

answers.text: They never come to know the truth
They never share what they learn

cards.text: Always learning, never getting there. It's like driving all day while your GPS says "recalculating" and never once says "You have arrived."
Then Paul names two men, Jannes and Jambres, who opposed Moses, Israel's leader. He says these men oppose the truth in just the same way.
Paul doesn't tiptoe around it, friend. He says these men are depraved in mind.

cards.question: Paul says the men who oppose the truth are still approved in the faith.
Paul says the men who oppose the truth will keep advancing further and further.
Just like with Jannes and Jambres, Paul says these men's folly will be ___ to everyone.
